original_text: Blood Platelets  Result from fragmentation of megakaryocytes Involved in blood clotting (coagulation) A blood clot consists of RBC s & Fibrin threads
explanation: Platelets (thrombocytes) are cell fragments formed by the fragmentation of large cells in the bone marrow called megakaryocytes. Platelets are essential for blood clotting (coagulation). A mature blood clot consists of a meshwork of insoluble fibrin threads that trap red blood cells (RBCs) to seal a damaged vessel.

questions.q: What cell type fragments to produce platelets in the bone marrow?
questions.exp: Platelets are formed from the cellular fragmentation of large bone marrow cells called megakaryocytes.

questions.q: What are the structural components of a blood clot?
opts: Red blood cells and fibrin threads
questions.exp: A blood clot consists of a network of sticky fibrin threads that trap red blood cells to block blood loss.
